title: Regional traffic surge, partial SLO degradation: incident analysis and corrective roadmap
creator: Asha Patel
description: On 2026-02-18 we observed a sudden traffic surge originating in EU-WEST that caused increased tail-latency and an SLO miss for text generation endpoints. Traffic was partially failed over to US regions which reduced availability for EU customers and exposed weaknesses in circuit breaker and load-shedding policies. This ticket documents the event timeline, root causes, immediate mitigations, and a prioritized corrective roadmap.
timeline: 2026-02-18 09:12 UTC — First alert: 95th percentile latency for /v1/generate (eu-west cluster) crossed 800ms (SLO target 300ms).
2026-02-18 09:14 UTC — Autoscaling triggered but observed slow VM provisioning due to burst cold-starts in dedicated pools.
2026-02-18 09:20 UTC — Circuit breaker for eu-west marked the region as unhealthy and routed ~40% of traffic to us-east as configured by smart routing.

2026-02-18 09:23 UTC — US region experienced increased load; KV cache miss rate spiked because cache keys were highly cardinal due to user-supplied prefixes, causing CPU contention and higher token cost.
2026-02-18 09:28 UTC — Load-shedding policy prioritized embedding workloads over generation; generation requests started queueing, increasing tail latency.
2026-02-18 09:35 UTC — On-call forced a partial rollback of a recent batching kernel change (PR #7321) to reduce CPU pressure in us-east.
2026-02-18 09:50 UTC — Manual soft-reset of eu-west circuit breaker and temporary raise of concurrency cap restored ~70% of eu-west traffic to local serving.
2026-02-18 11:05 UTC — Metrics stabilized; follow-up work tracked under this ticket.
2026-02-18 11:30 UTC — Page closed; post-incident analysis initiated.
2026-02-19 — Engineering review meeting: validated root causes and prioritized follow-ups.
impact: Transient SLO misses for generation (P95 and P99) in eu-west and higher cost due to cross-region serving; estimated customer-facing error/latency exposure window ~38 minutes, affecting ~2.3% of requests from EU customers during the event.
root_causes: Circuit breaker design was binary for region health (open/closed) with aggressive thresholds leading to large-scale failovers instead of graded throttling.
Autoscaling cooldowns and capacity pooling settings for dedicated pools delayed scale-up during a burst cold-start scenario.
Load-shedding prioritized embeddings ahead of generation inadvertently because of weight configuration mismatch in the policy engine.
KV cache ineffective for workload due to high prefix cardinality; cache thrash increased backend CPU and IO, amplifying latency under load.
A recently deployed batching kernel change increased CPU usage at medium sequence lengths; rollback helped but indicates insufficient canary/load testing for kernel changes.
Routing rules lacked a circuit-breaker-aware gradual-failover path (no soft-degrade band).
mitigations: Immediate: manual soft-reset of regional circuit breaker to allow graceful reconnection and raise local concurrency cap by 25% (09:50 UTC).
Immediate: rolled back batching kernel PR #7321 in us-east to relieve CPU pressure (09:35 UTC).
Immediate: temporarily adjusted load-shedding weights to favor generation for eu-west customer traffic (09:40 UTC).
Monitoring: added ad-hoc dashboards for KV cache hit-rate, per-prefix cardinality distribution, and cross-region failover ratios.
Customer comms: incident summary and timeline posted to status.redwood.com and notified top 10 impacted accounts.
follow_up_actions: ENG-10701 — Implement graded circuit-breaker states (green/yellow/red) and soft-throttle fallback instead of hard failover. Owner: Miguel Santos. Due: 2026-03-12.
ENG-10702 — Revise autoscaling cooldowns and add proactive 'surge-prewarm' for dedicated pools triggered by traffic slope detection. Owner: Lena Fischer. Due: 2026-03-05.
ENG-10703 — Update load-shedding policy engine to support per-workload SLAs and safe default weight mapping; add e2e tests. Owner: Rajiv Menon. Due: 2026-03-01.
ENG-10704 — Add KV cache audit: detect high prefix cardinality and auto-disable prefix-based caching, plus telemetry to alert at 10%+ unique-prefix spike. Owner: Priya Gupta. Due: 2026-02-28.
ENG-10705 — Strengthen PR canary requirements for kernel/public runtime changes: synthetic surge test in staging that simulates cross-region failover. Owner: SRE Team (rotating). Due: 2026-03-15.
ENG-10706 — Create a playbook for graded failover including thresholds, expected latency windows, and automated rollback triggers. Owner: On-call SRE lead. Due: 2026-03-08.
notes: Post-incident review (2026-02-19): PMs asked to review customer-facing SLA language to reflect graded failover behavior.
Design feedback: soft-fallback requires signal harmonization between routing, circuit-breaker, and autoscaler — agreed to add a small 'safety canary' token bucket for route migration.
SRE review: prioritize ENG-10704 (cache audit) as high ROI — cache thrash was the biggest amplifier of this event.
Cost note: cross-region serving added ~15% token-level cost for the event window; include cost analysis in ENG-10705 canary tests.
Next: split follow-up issues into two-week milestones; owners to provide weekly status in the reliability shiproom.
